meta.title: MCP Question Bank — Chapter 15: Versioning, 2026-07-28 Changelog & Feature Lifecycle

questions.question: What does an MCP version identifier like 2026-07-28 actually denote?

options.text: The date the documentation website was updated
A YYYY-MM-DD version label marking the last date backwards-incompatible changes were made to the specification
The server's build date
A semantic version in disguise

questions.explanation: MCP uses date-stamped string version identifiers (YYYY-MM-DD) indicating the last date of backwards-incompatible changes. 2026-07-28 replaced 2025-11-25.

questions.question: What is the single headline change of the 2026-07-28 revision?

options.text: A switch from JSON to Protocol Buffers
MCP became stateless at the protocol layer: no initialize handshake, no protocol-level sessions, so servers run behind ordinary load balancers and on serverless platforms
Mandatory paid licensing
Removal of the tools primitive

questions.explanation: Six SEPs together made MCP a request/response stateless protocol — the most requested change for reliability and scalability of remote servers.

questions.question: Which handshake did 2026-07-28 remove, and what replaced it?

options.text: The TLS handshake, replaced by QUIC
The initialize/notifications/initialized handshake, replaced by per-request _meta fields (protocolVersion, clientCapabilities, clientInfo) plus the mandatory server/discover RPC
OAuth consent, replaced by API keys
tools/list, replaced by server/discover

questions.explanation: SEP-2575: the handshake is gone; every request self-describes via _meta, servers should identify themselves via serverInfo in each result's _meta, and server/discover (which servers MUST implement) provides up-front version/capability discovery.

questions.question: What is the required resultType field introduced in 2026-07-28?

options.text: A MIME type for the payload

A discriminator on every result: "complete" for ordinary results, "input_required" for MRTR interim results (and "task" reserved for the Tasks extension); results from earlier-protocol servers that omit it are treated as "complete"
A boolean success flag
The name of the SDK that produced the result

questions.explanation: SEP-2322 made resultType required so clients can parse results polymorphically: complete vs input_required (MRTR), with 'task' reserved by the Tasks extension. Missing field from legacy servers → treat as complete.

questions.question: Which methods were removed outright in 2026-07-28?

options.text: tools/list and prompts/get
ping, logging/setLevel, and notifications/roots/list_changed (log level moved to per-request _meta; resources/subscribe & unsubscribe and the HTTP GET endpoint were replaced by subscriptions/listen)
elicitation/create
server/discover

questions.explanation: The changelog lists ping, logging/setLevel, and notifications/roots/list_changed as removed; logging is now per-request via io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel, and change notifications consolidated onto subscriptions/listen.

questions.question: Under the feature lifecycle policy adopted in 2026-07-28, what states can a specification feature be in, and what's the minimum deprecation window?

options.text: Alpha, Beta, GA — 30 days
Active, Deprecated, Removed — with a minimum twelve-month deprecation window and a registry of deprecated features
Draft, Final — no window
Experimental, Stable, Legacy — 6 months

questions.explanation: SEP-2596 defines Active/Deprecated/Removed, a minimum 12-month window (deprecated features keep working in this version and every version published within a year), and a deprecated-features registry. Actual removal needs a separate explicit proposal.

questions.question: SCENARIO: Your production server heavily uses Sampling. It's deprecated in 2026-07-28. Do you need an emergency migration before July 28?

options.text: Yes; deprecated features stop working on release day

No — deprecated features remain fully functional for at least the twelve-month window; nothing breaks on release day, but new implementations shouldn't adopt them and you should plan migration to direct LLM provider APIs
Only if you also use Roots
Sampling was removed, not deprecated

questions.explanation: Per the maintainers, 'nothing breaks on July 28': Roots, Sampling, and Logging (SEP-2577) keep working for at least twelve months. Migration paths: tool params/config for roots, direct LLM APIs for sampling, stderr/OpenTelemetry for logging.

questions.question: What changed about client registration in the 2026-07-28 authorization stack?

options.text: Registration is no longer required

Dynamic Client Registration (RFC 7591) was deprecated in favor of Client ID Metadata Documents (CIMD); DCR remains available for backwards compatibility with authorization servers that don't support CIMD
Only static pre-registration is allowed now
CIMD was deprecated in favor of DCR

questions.explanation: The changelog deprecates DCR as the registration mechanism: CIMD (URL-based client IDs proving domain control) is the way forward, with DCR kept for compatibility until a future removal.

questions.question: Which OAuth hardening did 2026-07-28 add regarding the iss parameter?

options.text: iss was removed from responses

Authorization servers SHOULD include iss in authorization responses (RFC 9207), and clients MUST validate a present iss against the recorded issuer before redeeming the authorization code — mitigating mix-up attacks
iss now carries the access token
Clients must ignore iss

questions.explanation: SEP-2468: issuer identification in authorization responses binds the response to the expected authorization server, preventing mix-up attacks where a code would be redeemed at an attacker's token endpoint.

questions.question: How did 2026-07-28 repartition the JSON-RPC server-error code range for MCP?

options.text: MCP now uses positive error codes

-32000 to -32019 stays implementation-defined (existing SDK usage grandfathered) and -32020 to -32099 is reserved for the MCP spec; draft codes were renumbered (HeaderMismatch → -32020, MissingRequiredClientCapability → -32021, UnsupportedProtocolVersion → -32022)
All errors collapsed into -32603
Error codes are now strings

questions.explanation: The error code allocation policy splits the JSON-RPC server-error range and renumbered the new errors accordingly; resource-not-found also moved from -32002 to -32602 to align with JSON-RPC Invalid Params.

questions.question: In the versioning docs and Inspector terminology, what defines the 'legacy' vs 'modern' protocol eras?

options.text: Legacy = stdio; modern = HTTP
Legacy uses the initialize handshake (2025-11-25 and earlier); modern uses per-request protocol metadata (2026-07-28 and later); dual-era implementations deliberately support both
Legacy = open source; modern = commercial
The eras differ only in default port numbers

questions.explanation: The era split: a modern-only client can't talk to a legacy-only server and vice versa — version negotiation detects the mismatch but doesn't bridge it. Dual-era servers answer the legacy initialize alongside server/discover, which is how nothing broke on release day.

questions.question: SCENARIO: Your remote MCP server must serve both a 2025-11-25 IDE plugin and a 2026-07-28 agent. What's the recommended approach?

options.text: Run two separate domains forever
Serve dual-era: answer the legacy initialize handshake alongside server/discover; SDKs route per request (e.g., by the MCP-Protocol-Version header or its absence) so one deployment handles both eras
Reject legacy clients with 426 Upgrade Required
Downgrade the server to legacy-only

questions.explanation: New-spec servers can be dual-era: SDKs route requests by the protocol version they name (legacy clients' initialize carries no modern header), so 2025-11-25 clients keep connecting while 2026-07-28 clients get the stateless path.

questions.question: What happened to the old HTTP+SSE transport in 2026-07-28?

options.text: It became the default transport
Already superseded since 2025-03-26, it was formally reclassified as Deprecated under the lifecycle policy with a year-long offramp; migrate to Streamable HTTP
It was renamed Streamable HTTP
It was extended with HTTP/3 support

questions.explanation: SEP-2596 reclassified the legacy HTTP+SSE transport as Deprecated. The includeContext values 'thisServer'/'allServers' were also reclassified as Deprecated in the same sweep.

questions.question: What observability convention did 2026-07-28 document for _meta?

options.text: A new binary tracing format
OpenTelemetry / W3C Trace Context propagation via the traceparent, tracestate, and baggage keys (SEP-414), so distributed traces correlate across host, SDK, server, and downstream calls
Mandatory Prometheus metrics
Logging every payload to stdout

questions.explanation: Locking down these _meta key names means a trace starting in a host application can follow a tool call through the client SDK, the MCP server, and downstream systems as a single span tree.

questions.question: SCENARIO: Under the SDK tiering system, what were Tier 1 SDKs expected to do during the ten-week release-candidate window (locked May 21, final July 28, 2026)?

options.text: Nothing; SDKs update whenever convenient
Ship support for the new specification within the validation window, so implementers could validate the changes against real workloads before the final release
Freeze all releases entirely
Rewrite themselves in Rust

questions.explanation: The RC window existed for SDK maintainers and client implementers to validate against real workloads; under the SDK tier system Tier 1 SDKs (TypeScript, Python, and peers) were expected to ship support within it — and all four spoke 2026-07-28 on release day.
